chapter_theme: Songs at Palani (பழநி, 4 of 7): the poet confesses bondage to courtesans who sell their bodies and take a man's wealth, the rotting body and its burning, and his own faults, and asks for Murugan's feet, grace and liberating knowledge; the praise turns on Murugan as Siva's teacher, as the Tamil saint who defeated the Jains, on Vishnu as uncle, and on the shrine's patron from Kalisai.
structure_note: Courtesan songs (149, 150, 152, 154, 155) and songs of women's charms (151, 161, 163); death and the body (154, 157, 158); a list of self-accusations (159); and three songs of doctrine and yoga rather than confession (156, 160, 162). Two songs (149, 152) name Seypathi (Vayalur) as the place where Murugan took the poet into service; three (149, 150) cast Murugan as the saint who impaled the Jains.

149.reading: The poet describes women who arrange their clothes and hair, chew betel, call a man to bed, cloud his sense, embrace him with nail-marked breasts and take the wealth of proud men while binding them in lust, and asks Murugan to end the delusion that drives his mind to the senses and give him his holy anklets. The praise makes Murugan the poet-king who impaled the Jain teachers on heated stakes, spread holy ash, and set his weighty word into fire and water; whom the moon-crowned Siva honoured as 'father'; and who stopped the poet at Seypathi and made him his servant, at Palani.
149.nuance: கைப்பொருட் கவர, taking the wealth in a man's hand, marks the women as courtesans; ப்ரமம், delusion, is the poet's word for his state. கனற்புனலிற் கனத்த சொலைப் பதித்தெழுதி points to the ordeals of fire and water by which, in tradition, Sambandar's written verses defeated the Jains of Madurai. தகப்பன் மதித்து உகப்பன் எனச் சிறக்க has Siva honour his son as a father, the teacher's rank. செய்ப்பதிக்குள் எனைத் தடுத்து அடிமைப் படுத்த is the poet's own story: he was stopped and taken into service at Vayalur.

150.reading: The poet describes women with musk-smeared breasts and moon-bright faces who coax, plead and deceive in one trade, claim a man as their right and charmingly take every possession, and asks that, through the sorrow and infatuation they cause, he may still come to praise Murugan's flower feet and gain grace, joy and kinship with him. The praise runs through Vishnu's deeds (the demoness Kamsa sent, the lion that devoured Hiranya, the one who drove Arjuna's chariot), a battle in drum syllables against an elephant-faced foe, the Jains impaled, the leaf that went against the river and the poem that brought a girl back from her bones, at Sivagiri.
150.nuance: பொருளுள தெவைகளு நயமொடு கவர்பவர், those who charmingly take whatever wealth there is, is the courtesan charge. உரை நதி எதிர்பட and என்பின் அரிவையை எதிர்வர விடுகவி are the leaf floating upstream in the Vaigai and the poem that raised a girl from her bones, both told of Sambandar, here credited to Murugan. Many runs of the rhythm (the list of Vishnu's names before மருகோனே, துங்கன் வஞ்சன் சங்கன் மைந்தன் தருமகன்) split uncertainly.

151.reading: The poet runs through a woman's beauty as a string of questions (is her hair darkness or cloud, her brow a bow or a crescent, her speech nectar or fruit, her breasts elephants or hills), says he gives his heart to such dancing sinful women, and asks instead for the glory of a scripture that thinks only of Murugan's two red feet. The praise names the vel that cut down the asura chief, the gods and sages who serve him, Ganapati's brother, the hunter girl's husband and Kathirkamam, at Palani.
151.nuance: The doubting similes (இருளோ புயலோ, சிலையோ பிறையோ) are the stock catalogue of beauty, and the dance syllables (திந்தித் திமிதிமி) belong to the women's dance, not to battle. மறையாகிய சீர் may mean the glory of scripture or of a secret; the sense of the plea is not certain. Kathirkamam (கதிர்காமா) is named in a Palani song.

152.reading: The poet describes courtesans adorned with saffron, camphor, sandal, coral and garlands who sell their breasts for a price, and asks not to delight in their sinful words sweet as milk, sugar and honey, but to keep the love Murugan gave him at Seypathi of singing Thiruppugazh daily with his lotus feet held within. The praise names the vel that dried the sea, bowed the eight hills, burst Krauncha and crushed Sura, and the guru loved by the father who drank the poison and dances in the burning ground wearing the gods' bones, at Avinankudi with its golden-pot towers.
152.nuance: பணைத்தனம் விற்கும் பொதுமாதர், women who sell their breasts, is the plainest courtesan charge of the book. The song names its own book: ஓதுகின்ற திருப்புகழ் நித்தம் பாடும் அன்பு, the love of singing Thiruppugazh daily, given at Seypathi (Vayalur), where by tradition the poet received his calling.

153.reading: The poet describes in detail lovemaking with women, from the sweating face and loosened hair to the bird-cries of the throat and the sound of bangles and anklets, and says that even if he falls into that river of pleasure he, Murugan's servant, will never for a moment forget his feet. The praise names the war against the asuras in the sea, Murugan's courtship of the hunter girl in the millet field, and the peacock that circled the world while the elephant-faced one circled Siva, and the lord in the heart of the servant from Kalisai, at Veerai and Palani, the hill of knowledge.
153.nuance: The plea is unusual: not to be freed from women but, even while falling (வீழுகினும்), not to forget the feet (மறவேனே). ஆனைமுகர் அரனை ஓடி வலம்வரு முன் ... உலகை வலமாக வரு மயில் is the race round the world for the fruit, told fully in 176. கலிசை வரு சேவகன், the servant from Kalisai, recurs in the Palani songs (158, 159) as a devotee in whose heart Murugan lives.

154.reading: The poet describes adorned women who clutch a man, then his life after them: worry, wealth gone, stammering speech, a staff, disease, exhaustion and the sickbed, until many bind the body, beat their heads, lay it on the cremation logs and burn it to ash, and asks whether he will become a mere corpse. The praise, after a battle in drum syllables, names the deeds of Siva who burned the cities and Kama and the punishment of Brahma, Murugan as the true guru who taught the meaning to the supreme dancer, and his union with the parrot-voiced girl, at Palani.
154.nuance: The confession moves in one breath from the women's embrace (கொளுமாதர் சுகமுற்று) to ruin, old age and the pyre, so that lust leads straight to the burning ground; சடமாமோ, 'shall I become a corpse?', is the whole plea. பரமர்க்குச் சற்குருவொத்துப் பொருளைக் கற்பித்தருள்வோனே is Murugan teaching Siva. Who does the acts before it (knocking out the sun's teeth, burning the cities, burning Kama, striking Brahma) depends on how the run is parsed; most are Siva's deeds.

155.reading: The poet describes priced women who sing in the street, call out 'who has come?', bathe, take a man to the cotton bed, rouse lust with charms and, when he begs, shut the front door, and asks Murugan to remove his desire for them and give his golden feet. The praise names Krishna, who had Arjuna drive the chariot as a eunuch and gave the Pandavas Kurukshetra through friendship, as uncle, and Murugan as the guru who spoke the quality into Siva's ear, at Palani of cool Tamil.
155.nuance: பொன் பறி விலைமாதர், priced women who snatch gold, and முன்றலை வாயில் அடைத்து, shutting the door, mark the courtesan: the door closes when the money ends. ஒரு பேடி இன்கன தேரை நடத்தி recalls Arjuna as Brihannala. சங்கரனார் செவி புக்கப் பண்பு does not name Om, so `gnaanam` stands for what was taught.

156.reading: A short song: Murugan, the guru who spoke the instructing mantra into both of Siva's ears to cool his heart, the son of Sivakama Sundari, is asked to come and say 'do not fear' to one who, not loving his deeds, wanders the world in vain in base illusion, and to give the bliss of grace-knowledge so that understanding grows and trouble ends. The praise names Krishna who stole butter and was tied to the mortar, Rama as uncle, Devayanai and the hunter girl, at Thiruvavinankudi.
156.nuance: The song opens with the teaching (உபதேச மந்த்ரம் இரு செவிமீதிலும்) and asks for the same gift for the poet: அருள்ஞான இன்பம். அவமாயை, base illusion, is the condition. செகமேல் மெய் கண்ட may mean 'who saw the truth in the world' or allude to Meykandar of the Siddhanta; I can't tell.

157.reading: The poet pictures death: drums beat, Death's men seize him and drag him with a rope, kin wail, the body is burned and the ashes sent to the sea; before this hut is gone, he asks that, as the Veda describes the final state of release, body, life and faculties be passed beyond and the three gunas brought under, and that Murugan come dancing on the peacock and give him Siva's feet. The praise tells how Siva praised him, how the worlds shook as he chased the serpent, his union with the hunter girl in the millet hut, and how he taught Agastya the ways of knowledge and penance in Tamil, at Palani.
157.nuance: The plea is for release while still in the body (படிக்குடிலை ஒழியாதே, before the earthly hut is gone), described in Vedantic terms: மறைமுறையின் இறுதிநிலை முத்தி, கரணவெளி, குணத்திரயம். குறுமுநிவன் is Agastya; Murugan as his Tamil teacher recurs through the book. The middle lines of the plea split uncertainly.

158.reading: The poet describes the body as an illusory mass of filth, pus, blood, worms, skin, flesh, bone and nerves, food for jackals, vultures and crows, that stinks the moment the life passes to Yama's hand, and confesses that, cherishing it as lasting, he desires women and is dying in that sorrow; he asks Murugan to love him. The praise names Krishna who broke the two tusks of the elephant sent by Kamsa and herded cows with his flute, the vel that broke Krauncha, and the servant from Kalisai who bows to Murugan, at Veerai and Palani.
158.nuance: The catalogue of the body (சீ, உதிரம், புழு, தோல், தசை, எலும்பு, நரம்பு) is the Naladiyar's method, turned on the poet's own body and set beside his desire: he knows what the body is and still cherishes it (பேணி நிலையென்று). The elephant whose tusks Krishna broke (வாரண இரண்டு கோடொடிய) is Kuvalayapida, by its details.

159.reading: The poet lists his own faults: an angry fool, a wrongdoer without order, a deceiver who seeks the disease of birth, without justice or worth, a liar to all, cruel, a talebearer, ignorant, rubbish who does not cherish Murugan's feet; and asks that even so he be joined to Murugan's devotees. The praise names the victory garland of the war, the peacock as horse, the servant from Kalisai in whose heart he lives, at Veerai and Palani.
159.nuance: The whole confession is self-abuse without a story (சீறல் அசடன், கபடி, கோளன், கூளன்), and the plea is modest: not release but company, உனடியரொடு கூடும் வகைமை.

160.reading: A song of doctrine: Murugan is addressed as the one life that is the silence at the crown of the Veda, Siva as knowledge, the non-dual supreme flame and the formless nature; the poet confesses that, not knowing how to reach the lotus feet of bliss known to the liberated who have seen turiya, he takes as real the body formed in the womb from seed and breath, divided by the three gunas and stirred by deeds, a cave of illusion, and asks for grace to rule this worthless thing. The praise names him as root, crown and middle of the six religions and the Veda, the cosmic egg and space, the guru who came as the pranava mantra, the dancer on the peacock and Saravanabhava, Subramanya on Palani hill.
160.nuance: The vocabulary is Vedanta and Siddhanta together: சுருதிமுடி மோனம், அத்துவிதம், நிட்கள சொரூபம், துரியநிலை, முக்குண விபாகம். The body is born in the womb (கருவில் உரு, சுக்கில நிதானம், வளி பொரும) and is called refuse (குப்பைமல வாழ்வு) and a cave of maya. உருபிரணவாம் மந்த்ர ... குருநாதா makes Murugan the pranava in person. Several compounds split uncertainly.

161.reading: The poet confesses that, enslaved to women, he took Kama's treatise of lovemaking as if it were scripture and mixed with fools, and asks that, like Murugan's devotees, he may meditate on the scriptures, walk Manu's path, know understanding by understanding, become full, and drink unceasingly the nectar of true knowledge and bliss. The praise tells the Rama story through Sugriva, Hanuman and Vibhishana's crowning and Ravana's burning with his kin, and names Murugan Rama's nephew, the hunter girl's lord, at Palani, the joy of the mountain's daughter.
161.nuance: மதனூலே சுருதியென நினைந்து, taking the love-treatise for the Veda, is the poet's sharpest self-mockery: the wrong book taken as scripture, set against அருமறைகளே நினைந்து. அறிவை அறிவால் அறிந்து, knowing knowledge by knowledge, is the goal.

162.reading: A song of yoga: the poet asks that his senses gather and reach the land without moon or sun, climb the mountain of Namasivaya, let the bliss of the tongue fall like a waterfall, play among the nadas, forget body, souls, delusion and 'I', become one end with the Lord, and ride on great knowledge around the worlds. The praise names Siva with konrai, moon and river in his hair, 'my father', and his consort as the pure lord's half, Murugan on the peacock that shattered forests and seas, and Kama's arrows shamed, at 'our Palani'.
162.nuance: The plea is a yogic ascent, not a confession: வான் இந்து கதிர் இலாத நாடு (where neither moon nor sun shines), நமசிவாய வரை, நாவின்ப ரசம், நாதங்களொடு குலாவி, நான் என்பது அறிவிலாமல். ஓமங்கி உருவமாகி and இருவோரும் ஓரந்த மருவி (the two joining in one end) are uncertain splits; who the two are is not said. The last lines of praise are hard to parse.

163.reading: The poet says that fate, written on his head, drove him into houses with fragrant-haired women whose eyes are nets, and that he sinks in a burning sea of attachment to sons, mother, father, wives, friends and cattle; he asks for the meaning that is first as A is first, to join his hands and melt crying 'Hara', and for Murugan's feet, coming on the emerald peacock with vel and cock banner. The praise runs through Krishna's deeds (the hill as umbrella, Vidura's house, the stolen butter, Vamana, the dance on the serpent) as uncle, and Murugan who brought the elephant to frighten the girl among the deer, guru, son of the mountain's daughter, at Palani.
163.nuance: விதி தலையில் எழுதியும் places the poet's lust under fate. The bonds of kin (தனயர் அனை மதர் மனைவியர்) are a sea of fire (தவன சலதி). அகர முதல் உள பொருள் echoes the Kural's first line and points, as in 173, to the meaning of the first letter. வனிதை வெருவ முன் வர is the elephant that frightened Valli into Murugan's arms.

links.note: Both name Seypathi (Vayalur) as the place where Murugan acted on the poet: in 149 he stopped him and made him his servant, in 152 he gave him the love of singing Thiruppugazh daily. Read together they are the book's account of its own beginning.

Both hear the funeral drums and see the body covered and the fire taken up. The Naladiyar ends in irony, the dying carrying the dead; 157 asks for release before that hour comes, while the hut of the body still stands.

Both take the body apart into blood, bone, nerves, skin and flesh. The Naladiyar asks which part is the woman one desires; 158 turns the list on the poet's own body and confesses that, knowing this, he still desires women.

Both place the soul's bondage at conception: Tirumular has maya join the soul in the womb, turiya broken and karma take hold; 160 has the form grow in the womb from seed and breath, divided by the three gunas and covered in deceit, and contrasts it with the turiya state of the liberated.

The Kural's first line makes A the first of letters as the Lord is first of the world; 163 borrows the words (அகர முதல்) and asks for the meaning that is first in that way, the secret that 173 says Murugan told Siva.

source_issues: Song 150: the long run of names in lines 44 to 46 of the praise (துங்கன் வஞ்சன் சங்கன் மைந்தன் தருமகன் முநி தழல் வருதகர்) does not split cleanly; possibly garbled.
Song 156: தெவயானை (line 13) for தேவயானை, probably a lost vowel sign.
Song 161: one corrupt character in மதனு஡லே (line 2); clearly மதனூலே (Kama's treatise).
Song 162: சீரங் னெனது (line 10) looks garbled, a letter lost after சீரங்.
